candidate.title: SUPeR-seq
candidate.scope: Illumina schematic-level SUPeR-seq (single-cell universal poly(A)-independent RNA sequencing), interpreted using the Fan et al. 2015 implementation. The full image was inspected: the RNA Low-Level Detection heading covers a complete SUPeR-seq row, an adjacent scRNA-seq row, and a partially clipped MATQ-seq row; a clipped chemical-structure panel lies at the right. The assigned card selects the SUPeR-seq row. The other named rows are separate catalogue workflows, not alternatives or components within that row. Within SUPeR-seq, the upper native-poly(A)+ and lower poly(A)- RNA routes are both in scope. They depict target classes within a single-cell preparation, not an evidenced physical separation into fractions. Each class retains its own transformation provenance under the common captions. The drawing ends at purified RNA-derived DNA; the primary paper identifies this as amplified cDNA used subsequently for Illumina DNA library preparation. Unshown library construction, sequencing, validations and computational analysis are interfaces/readout interpretation only, not added operations.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and row label identify SUPeR-seq. All four depicted captions apply to both the upper poly(A)+ and lower poly(A)- routes. Separate local operation instances track the two material classes without claiming that they were isolated or processed in separate vessels; the primary paper explicitly describes simultaneous detection from one cell. The original 2015 method resolves primer identity and the condensed cDNA-conversion block. Its broader poly(A)- applicability includes circular RNA, but the schematic does not draw a separate circRNA-specific preparation. Random priming permits these target classes without establishing exhaustive recovery or identical capture of all RNA species. The adjoining scRNA-seq and MATQ-seq rows do not expand this assigned card into a grouped extraction.
